function: Joint beamforming and movable-antenna position design by a TD3 agent, minimizing the target-angle CRB under user SINR and power constraints in an ISAC base station (p. 1, p. 3)
system: 16-antenna monostatic DFRC base station with movable antennas serves K=4 single-antenna users and one target, single-antenna sensing receiver; 30 GHz; no RIS (p. 1, p. 4)
method: TD3 deep reinforcement learning (off-policy actor-critic, replay buffer), trained by interaction with a simulated environment; reward combines the CRB-related term and an SINR penalty (p. 3)
data_channel: Custom simulated far-field multipath channel, random gains CN(0,1) and angles U(0,pi), 3 paths; closed-form crosstalk model from [7]; no standard channel model or dataset (p. 2, p. 4)
test_conditions: One random-channel simulation; no separate train/test scenarios described; results swept over SNR (-10 to 20 dB) and movable-region size (7.5 to 20 wavelengths) (p. 4, p. 5)
baselines: Non-learned: random beamforming on fixed half-wavelength ULA (FPA+RBF). Learned variants of the proposed method: TD3 with fixed array (FPA+TD3), TD3 without crosstalk modeling (MA+TD3) (p. 4)
metrics: Average CRB of target-angle estimation (dB) versus SNR and versus movable-region size; TD3 training reward convergence (p. 4, p. 5)
q1_support: p. 4: "the locations are generated through random channel realization" - custom simulator (field response vectors, Eqs. 1-2, p. 2); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "the average CRB variation versus the size of MA moving region" - a sweep of a design parameter (Fig. 4); no test on an unseen scenario, no fine-tuning or transfer is stated.
q3_support: p. 4: "MA+TD3 utilizes the proposed TD3 training without considering the antenna crosstalk" - FPA+RBF is non-learned, but FPA+TD3 and MA+TD3 are ablations of the proposed agent; no earlier learned method or other learning algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "offering a scalable solution for MA enabled ISAC" - qualitative claim only; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime is reported anywhere in the paper.
q5_support: p. 4: "Other simulation parameters are listed in Table I." - data are synthetic and generated by the authors; no code or data link or DOI, and no public dataset or measurement.
notes: PDF is the arXiv preprint 2509.03273v1 (3 Sep 2025), titled Crosstalk-Resilient Beamforming for Movable Antenna Enabled ISAC; it does not print the DOI, so the DOI-to-title match cannot be checked from the file. Movable antennas at the BS, no RIS. The agent outputs the ISAC precoder F jointly with antenna positions p (p. 3, Eq. 15), so I take the function as ISAC beamforming (area 5), not antenna hardware design; reviewer to confirm. All learned baselines are variants of the proposed scheme, hence q3=0.
